scope: Fresh independent review of the concrete, unpublished GitHub-native profile preview and the written future-website continuity plan. The website is not built, and prior mascot scores are not carried over as application approval.
independence: Saved before reading any other new GitHub independent review. No browser, research, other agent or source mutation used.

scoreMeaning: Ordinal expert craft score out of 10 for this current native profile application: strong, clear owner attribution and coherent warm identity, with modest editorial repetition. It is not a recognition rate, emotional-attachment result, future-website score or a direct rescore of the mascot rig.
confidence: Moderate-high for the inspected static hierarchy, copy and theme/size treatment. No empirical confidence claim for visitor behavior. The evidence is an explicitly labelled local preview, not a published-account audit.
strengths: Nag is clearly the human author in the actual preview: the day avatar sits beside Nagarjuna Boddu and heyNag; the README then says 'Hey, I'm Nag' and uses first person. The moth reads as a companion mark rather than an unnamed speaker claiming the projects.

The same cream face and unequal chartreuse paddles connect avatar and header across both themes. Using the day avatar consistently avoids requiring recognition of faint night-avatar stems. At the shown 320px profile size, name and face remain visible together.

The banner's small full-body moth does not have to communicate a precise emotion or invitation. The large heyNag wordmark and plain introduction carry the identity; the smile supplies a restrained welcoming tone.

Three named projects have concrete functions and direct personal heyNag destinations. 'Unofficial' and 'evolving experiment' set useful maturity/relationship expectations, while the private-work sentence prevents the public sample from pretending to represent everything Nag makes.

Wheel-scrolled 320px views show readable descriptions and a legible native pin list in the inspected themes. The render record reports no document-width overflow across 320–1440px and both selected header variants. This is suitable local application evidence, not physical-phone or public-delivery proof.

The continuity plan preserves clear human authorship, real work visible without mascot interaction, unchanged anatomy, static/reduced-motion paths and no unfinished website link. Those are appropriate constraints for a later built website review.

deductions.classification: Observed repetition, not measured abandonment or comprehension failure
deductions.finding: The bio and first README paragraph repeat substantially the same software/systems, useful-tools, curiosity and care-for-feel introduction. On the narrow view, the README repeats that general positioning across several lines before the specific public work begins. The project descriptions provide more individual detail than the duplicated opening.
deductions.improvementCriterion: In a later copy pass, keep the short bio self-contained and make the README opening add one distinct, verified perspective or shorten it. Compare the resulting native reading view; do not invent career claims or force the projects above GitHub's own profile chrome.
deductions.confidence: High that the repetition exists; unknown effect on readers.

recommendations: Accept the current profile as a coherent local application, subject to the later explicit shared team decision and the user's actual publication authorization. No source change is required by this review.
Keep the universal day avatar, theme-paired static header, first-person authorship, modest project maturity language and only personal heyNag destinations.

Treat the continuity plan's 'establish the shared identity immediately' wording as design intent, not a demonstrated human-recognition result. A future record should distinguish visible association cues from tested recognition.

When the website is built, show Nag and real work before requiring mascot interaction; use Investigate & share to direct attention toward actual project detail. Reassess attribution in the built layout rather than assuming that asset reuse proves recognition.

continuityAssessment.currentProfile: The inspected application visibly links the moth, heyNag, Nag's full name and concrete software projects. This is a credible basis for continuity.
continuityAssessment.planQuality: The written contract is coherent: consistent names/assets/palette, first-person voice, factual project continuity, owner-cleared private-work stories, and reciprocal links only once a useful website exists.
continuityAssessment.notBuilt: No website page, interaction, reduced-motion implementation or cross-surface recognition outcome is reviewed here. The plan is not approved built artwork.
continuityAssessment.researchBoundary: Recognition of the same maker across GitHub and a website, emotional warmth, attachment and delayed owner/project recall remain hypotheses. Native badges, contribution counts and the local preview banner are context, not authored proof of those outcomes.

unscoredOutcomes.reason: No new unfamiliar-human responses or built website evidence. Current screenshots are local proposed fields/README/assets inside GitHub's DOM, not applied account changes or verified live publication.
